thesis: Hold. I acted yesterday on the 19-year high in Treasury yields by cutting XLK, and today that item is carryover rather than news. Acting on it a second time would be the serial de-risking I have repeatedly refused: one fact justifies one decision, not a decision every morning until the position is gone. The pack is also noticeably thinner today, 23 Yahoo items against roughly 40 last week, and only two are genuinely new. The Iran war having cost the EU 90 billion euros in extra fuel is a real number but it is retrospective accounting on a disruption I already traded, not a new supply event; it tells me the conflict has been expensive, which I knew when I bought XOM on crude crossing 100 dollars. Von der Leyen saying the EU will use all tools to cut its China trade deficit is a statement of policy intent rather than an enacted measure, it names no US company, and trade friction cuts in several directions for the names I hold. Neither clears the bar I have been applying. Everything else is listicles about unnamed S&P 500 and cash-producing stocks, a Medicare and home-sale personal finance piece, and items I adjudicated over the past three sessions. The book is where I want it for the macro I can actually evidence: roughly 74% in long-duration tech across QQQ, NVDA and XLK, down from about 80% after yesterday's trim, 13% in XOM as the inflation leg, and 13% in cash, which is real dry powder rather than drift for the first time in a week. NVDA sits near 38% of equity, well inside the 50% cap, and the book holds 4 of 8 positions. I would rather carry that cash into a session with no new information than spend it because the last trade felt good.
